title: Fork and ship current-session Agents
description: Adopt an owned fork of nicobailon/pi-subagents as the current-session multi-Agent engine. Preserve its mature child-Pi process, durable lifecycle, steering, resume, recovery, capability ceiling, and worktree foundations. Recast the public behavior around Claude Code: the main conversation may delegate automatically, background work is normal, direct child summaries stay compact, and the user can inspect, steer, stop, and resume from the accepted roster and Command Dialog. Tintinweb remains observable UI reference only; none of its code is adopted.
acceptance_criteria: The exact owned-fork source revision, npm archive identity, MIT license, and local delta are recorded. The main Agent can launch one or several fresh child Agents automatically in foreground or background, with bounded session-wide depth/concurrency/total accounting, stable identities, compact direct-child returns, durable current-session lifecycle, independent cancellation, acknowledged steering, safe resume, and optional per-Agent worktree isolation that never deletes changed work. The destructive-command circuit breaker applies to every child and requests that need a person reach the root session without an invisible wait. A quiet below-editor roster shows main plus direct children; Down from an empty editor selects, Enter opens a full-width non-floating Agent Command Dialog, and the same surface supports transcript inspection, steer, stop, resume, and nested detail. Normal and 64-column layouts preserve the editor and coordinate with Todo/BTW. The fork exposes no stock Fleet overlay/statusline, package settings UI, saved chains, scheduler, watchdog, memory, sharing, Agent Teams, Dynamic Workflows, or LSP. Aggregate, exact package, Pi 0.83 real Host, concurrent provider, crash/recovery, permission, worktree, focus restoration, and native PTY tests pass.
close_reason: Owned current-session Agents fork shipped and fully certified against the accepted Claude-style capability, UI, safety, and package contract.

title: Fork and ship the destructive-command circuit breaker
description: Adopt an owned fork of @gotgenes/pi-permission-system 24.0.0 from source commit 776ebcc764ca6c720b1f7eb430007de06f145b5f. Keep its mature Bash parsing, path resolution, policy engine, and forwarding infrastructure, but make normal Pi work unrestricted by default. The Capability intervenes only for a deliberately narrow family of destructive deletion and Git-discard commands, uses Pi Stuff's shared non-floating Command Dialog, and supplies the safety authority that tool-capable child Agents will inherit.
acceptance_criteria: Reads, edits, ordinary shell commands, tests, and ordinary project work run without Pi Stuff approval. Explicit safe deletions inside the current working directory run silently. A statically resolved deletion outside that directory or a tested Git command that discards uncommitted work asks once for that exact operation. Deleting the filesystem root, resolved user home, current working directory, Git worktree root, or all of their contents is denied. Destructive targets hidden behind unresolved variables, substitutions, unsafe broad globs, unsupported wrappers, or parse failure are denied with a concrete rewrite reason. Project/Agent content cannot relax the circuit breaker. Default startup writes no files and records no command log. The prompt is a full-width non-floating blocking Command Dialog that names the operation, restores prior Suite chrome, and creates no statusline. The fork preserves exact license/provenance and publishes through the Suite package gate. Pi 0.83 Host, normal/narrow PTY, adversarial command-shape, path, reload/shutdown, package, and public-safety tests pass. No LSP or OS sandbox is introduced.

comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text:
Final implementation decision and evidence, 2026-08-02 — Ship an owned fork of @juicesharp/rpiv-btw 2.3.1, preserving its MIT license, npm archive identity, source revision, and an explicit UPSTREAM delta record. The fork retains the useful parent-context conversion and independent streaming call, but narrows the product to Claude-style one-shot use: `/btw <question>` opens one full-width divider-led non-floating Command Dialog; there is no follow-up composer, tool access, normal transcript entry, statusline, notification, widget, or floating window. Bare `/btw` reopens the newest successful exchange. Successful display history is session-isolated, process-local, capped at 20, and exposes at most five earlier entries; it is never model input or durable session data. Historical images are omitted. Errors and provider-originated cancellation remain visible; user close/cancel never touches the main Agent.

The request snapshots Pi's compaction-aware effective context at invocation, removes a trailing pending assistant entry, applies a structured byte budget to text/thinking/tool stubs, disables tools, keeps an independent abort signal, retries context overflow once after clearing first-attempt partial output, and never rereads a changed main branch. Pi 0.83 has no public transcript-free Host model-call path. The fork therefore resolves the active registered model plus provider authentication through Pi, then calls the provider transport directly. This preserves model/auth selection and isolation but bypasses Host provider lifecycle/context hooks and Host retry/transport settings. That limitation is documented and tracked separately as ps-5cb.3; it does not justify a Pi fork.

A shared @jczhang02/pi-stuff-ui Capability Package now owns the Suite's only custom Command Dialog host. It is a logical singleton per Extension event bus even when npm physically bundles multiple copies. It serializes normal surfaces and FIFO blocking surfaces, restores the exact editor draft/footer/working row/Suite chrome before promises settle, survives synchronous close/throw/reentrant show, rejects late work during shutdown/reload, and never creates an overlay. Todo participates only through this shared chrome contract; its expand and all-complete linger state continue while temporarily suppressed.

Release engineering is part of the accepted implementation: UI, Todo, BTW, then Aggregate are packed by pinned Bun 1.3.14 into exact tarballs with SHA-256/SHA-512 manifest binding; certification exercises those same bytes through standalone installs, Aggregate loading, real Pi 0.83 RPC, and native PTY. Publication refuses unversioned work or pending Changesets, compares registry integrity, and publishes only a private read-only snapshot created by hashing and copying the same in-memory bytes, eliminating source-tarball replacement between certification and publish. System npm and Changesets publication are intentionally excluded because they repack Bun workspaces incorrectly.

Acceptance evidence: `bun run check` passed formatting, strict TypeScript, 116 tests/361 assertions, dependency audit, generated-output audit, public-safety audit, exact release-artifact certification, real Pi 0.83 Host loading, isolated provider behavior, transcript isolation, focus/chrome restoration, and native 100×32 plus 64×28 PTY flows. Independent UI/race and packaging/exact-bytes audits found no remaining blocker.

title: Define the Pi Stuff product capability set
description:
## Purpose

Decide which user-visible capabilities belong in the default Pi Stuff installation before selecting upstream Pi Packages or implementing any Capability.

This epic records the product interview, confirmed decisions, open questions, Package research, and final inclusion/exclusion decisions. It does not authorize implementation.

## Confirmed decisions

1. Pi Stuff is personal-first. It may remain publicly usable, but it is selected for the maintainer's own daily workflow rather than for every possible Pi user.
2. A third-party capability may be adopted only through an owned fork whose source is incorporated into the Pi Stuff monorepo as part of the Suite. Direct dependence on the original Package is not the target model.
3. Owned forks preserve upstream provenance, the upstream revision, applicable licenses, and a visible record of local changes. Product direction and release timing belong to Pi Stuff; low divergence from upstream is not a goal by itself.
4. The previous `jczhang02/pi-agent` repository is evidence for capability inventory and user experience only. Its code must not be copied, ported, translated, or otherwise used as implementation input.
5. A normal Pi Stuff installation should be immediately useful with a coherent default set of features, without requiring the user to enable and configure each one first.
6. Additional agents may be started automatically when useful; the user should not have to request every delegation manually.
7. Product decisions must be discussed through concrete usage scenarios and plain language. Unexplained implementation or product jargon is not an acceptable decision interface.
8. Large capability directions must be chosen before detailed UI behavior, Package selection, or implementation planning.

## Open decisions

- Which large user-visible capability directions belong in Pi Stuff?
- Which concrete daily workflows should each direction enable?
- Which directions are part of the default installation, optional, or excluded?
- Which existing Pi Packages are credible candidates for each accepted direction?
- Which candidate should be forked after comparing actual behavior, maintenance, adoption, license, compatibility, and source quality?
- What user experience should unify the selected forks?

## Process

1. Resolve one user decision at a time using concrete scenarios.
2. Append every confirmed decision to this epic.
3. Research facts rather than asking the user to supply them.
4. Search and compare Pi Packages only after the corresponding large capability direction is accepted.
5. Do not create implementation work until the user confirms that the product set is understood.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed large capability directions, default/optional/excluded choices, candidate Package comparisons, fork selections, and unresolved questions are recorded; the user explicitly confirms shared understanding before implementation work is created.
notes:
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Work-process management belongs in the default installation. During long work, Pi Stuff must show current, pending, blocked, and completed tasks; let the user add, cancel, or reorder work; answer BTW side questions without stopping the main task; continue owned work in the background; and notify the user when work completes or needs input.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — UI quality is a first-class default product direction, not merely a consistency layer for new Pi Stuff features. Pi Stuff may substantially reshape any user-visible presentation reachable without forking or modifying Pi itself, including built-in tool-call/result display, transcript presentation, diffs, test and error output, status/footer areas, Agent and task views, commands, and settings screens. The non-negotiable boundary is that Pi remains the Host and Pi core is not forked.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — Cross-session project and work memory belongs in the default installation. On returning to a repository, Pi Stuff should retain useful commands, important structure and conventions, prior investigations and failed approaches, user preferences, unfinished work, and key decisions preserved through long-conversation compression. Remembered information must be visible to the user and support correction and deletion.
Confirmed 2026-08-01 — End-to-end development work belongs in the default installation. Given a concrete issue, Pi Stuff should be able to read the issue and discussion, investigate and modify code, run the project's tests/lint/typecheck/build, inspect its own diff, obtain an additional-agent review, prepare commit and pull-request text, and inspect and repair CI failures. Confirmed operating rule 2026-08-01 — For the remaining Pi Stuff product and UI work, Claude Code is the default behavioral and visual reference. The Agent should independently research current released Claude Code behavior and official documentation, use source inspection only to recover decision details under the already-recorded no-copy independent-implementation boundary, translate the result to public Pi APIs, and make routine product decisions without asking the maintainer item by item. Direct translation remains constrained by all existing Suite rules: do not fork Pi Host; reject floating windows and overlays; keep conversation-first progressive disclosure; avoid duplicate state; use owned pinned forks for adopted Package capabilities; and record every resulting decision in Beads. The maintainer should be asked only when Claude Code has no clear precedent, when its behavior conflicts with a confirmed Pi Stuff constraint, when two viable directions create materially different daily workflows, or when the choice introduces a meaningful cost, privacy, external-action, compatibility, or ownership tradeoff. Material departures from Claude should receive concrete native Pi or HTML evidence before requesting a decision. This rule authorizes autonomous decision-making and documentation, not implementation of the product capability set before product scope is confirmed.
Confirmed Claude-first background-Agent lifecycle, 2026-08-01 — Pi Stuff has exactly three owners for Agent information: the conversation keeps durable launch and grouped terminal outcomes; the one-line vertical roster below the editor shows current session state; the full-width non-floating Agent Command Dialog owns conversation inspection, reply, stop, resume, error detail, partial result, and full result. Completion, failure, and stop never steal editor focus. Their terminal roster rows remain while the user reviews the current main response, then disappear on the next main-session user submission; x dismisses a finished row earlier. The durable conversation record remains. A selected running or waiting Agent can be stopped with x without a second confirmation popup; explicit roster selection is the guard, and state passes through stopping to stopped. Failures must name the shortest useful reason, preserve partial-result availability, and never render as success. Child-to-supervisor questions are internal coordination first: the main Agent should answer automatically when possible. Only after the main Agent decides a human choice is required does Pi Stuff show a persistent attention row above Todo and mark the child waiting; a non-empty editor retains focus and keystrokes, and the question is not duplicated into Todo. A permission request is distinct: it names the requesting Agent and action, temporarily owns the same Command Dialog, and Esc denies only that tool call rather than stopping the Agent. One Suite UI coordinator must own custom editor, widgets, footer, and non-overlay custom surface so permission can suspend BTW and restore the exact prior BTW or main draft; unrelated third-party dialogs cannot be reliably preempted and must be waited out. The native Pi 0.83 spike proves these focus, restoration, stop, mixed-state, and 64x28 layout paths through public APIs, so no Pi fork is required. Production lifecycle transport will use stable event IDs, origin-group IDs, durable terminal results, reload reconciliation, cross-process claiming, idempotent delivery, and no replayed OS notification after recovery. Whether Pi Stuff also ships a global Claude-style allow/ask/deny policy is a separate product decision. Evidence: docs/research/work-background-notification-ui-reference.md, docs/prototypes/tui/work-agent-lifecycle-spike-report.html, and work-agent-lifecycle-{machine,spike,spike-fixture,spike-capture.sh}.
Permission Capability research snapshot, 2026-08-01 — A global Claude-style allow/ask/deny layer is a real product decision rather than a UI detail: default-on means ordinary reads/searches proceed quietly while file modifications and effectful commands pause for a named approval; default-off preserves Pi current unrestricted flow and fewer interruptions. If the direction is accepted, the strongest fork base is conditionally @gotgenes/pi-permission-system 24.0.0 at commit 776ebcc764ca6c720b1f7eb430007de06f145b5f: MIT, about 31.3k npm downloads in the audited 30-day window, full policy/Bash/path/direct-child infrastructure, 2,672 upstream tests passing under Pi 0.83 dependencies, and real Pi 0.83 extension startup. It is also high-churn and maintainer-concentrated, with upstream defaults and UI unsuitable for the Suite. An owned fork must replace universal-ask with a useful Claude-like baseline; disable sensitive review logging by default; make global denies non-relaxable; keep dangerous modes user-owned; route prompts and native SettingsList through the shared non-floating coordinator; remove overlay/statusline UI; certify direct-child forwarding; and immediately deny unsupported nested child asks instead of waiting ten minutes. The composition is not yet end-to-end certified, and package adoption remains conditional on real-Host permission, reload, contention, trust, forwarding, recovery, and narrow-TUI acceptance tests. Current official Claude behavior and the genuine 2.1.220 capture agree that background child permission prompts surface in the main session, name the child, and Esc denies only that tool call. Evidence: docs/research/permission-capability-package-reference.md. No permission Capability selection is recorded yet.
Confirmed permission direction and fork base, 2026-08-01 — The maintainer selects B with an explicit amendment: Pi Stuff ships the permission infrastructure but defaults to unrestricted normal work. Reads, searches, code edits, normal writes, builds, tests, and ordinary shell commands proceed without confirmation. The common full-width non-floating permission surface appears only for destructive safety tripwires: deleting, overwriting, or moving existing content outside the current workspace; recursively removing the workspace/repository root; discarding uncommitted work through destructive Git operations; recursive ownership/permission changes outside the workspace; or targeting /home/jc, /, mounted filesystems, block devices, and equivalent catastrophic scopes. A destructive command whose target cannot be safely normalized because of unresolved variables, substitutions, unsafe globs, parse failure, or unsupported nested-Agent forwarding is denied with a reason so the Agent can rewrite it concretely instead of asking the user to approve an ambiguous command. Pi Stuff-owned temporary artifacts with recorded ownership may be cleaned without an outside-workspace prompt. Main and background Agents share the same rules and named request UI. Project files, Agent definitions, skills, MCP content, and child Agents cannot weaken the user-owned tripwires. Claude-like manual approval for ordinary edits and effectful commands remains an optional native-Settings mode, not the fresh-install default; neither mode adds a statusline. Pi Stuff will use an owned pinned fork of @gotgenes/pi-permission-system 24.0.0 at commit 776ebcc764ca6c720b1f7eb430007de06f145b5f as the permission kernel, subject to the documented Pi 0.83, direct-child, recovery, trust, safety-policy, and TUI acceptance gates. This permission layer is a tool-decision guard, not an OS sandbox. Evidence: docs/research/permission-capability-package-reference.md and docs/prototypes/tui/work-agent-lifecycle-spike-report.html.
Correction to the preceding permission note — The displayed /home/jc path is the shell-expanded value of the literal $HOME token in the product rule. The guard is defined against each running user's resolved home directory, not against one maintainer-specific path.
Feasibility correction to the selected permission direction, 2026-08-01 — The maintainer intent remains default-unrestricted work with rare intervention, but the preceding note's broad list overstates what a static tool gate can guarantee. Pi Stuff will call this a destructive-command circuit breaker, not a security boundary or a detector for every obviously wrong operation. The first certified policy covers only every registered Suite shell tool and a small tested family: rm, rmdir, unlink, find -delete, and common Git work-discard forms. Explicitly named deletion inside the session working directory runs silently unless it clears the directory as a whole. A statically resolved deletion outside the session working directory or a tested Git discard asks about the exact call once. Deleting /, the resolved $HOME, the session working directory, the Git worktree root, or an equivalent clear-all-contents target is denied without an approval option. Ambiguous destructive targets with unresolved variables, substitutions, unsafe globs, unrecognized wrappers, or parse failures are denied and returned to the Agent for a concrete rewrite. Tripwire approval is bound to the exact tool, arguments, cwd, Agent, and request ID and creates no session or persistent allow rule. The earlier Pi Stuff temporary-artifact exemption is withdrawn from the first release. The circuit breaker must run before unrestricted mode, project/Agent/session rules, child policy, and external authorizers; project content cannot weaken it. Every Suite shell-like tool must register for the same gate or fail certification. Direct-child behavior remains unclaimed until end-to-end certified. Interpreter-internal deletion, generated scripts, arbitrary MCP/Extension side effects, shell functions/aliases, symlink races, and all equivalent command forms are outside the guarantee; this remains distinct from an OS sandbox. Broader move, overwrite, chmod/chown, mount, and block-device protections may be added only after explicit detection and adversarial tests, not promised in advance.

The selected owned-fork base is pi-hermes-memory 0.9.2 at commit 5aafe2ca04cb55b62204b159389c8381894038ce (MIT), subject to implementation acceptance. It is the strongest native base among the audited candidates: about 19.4k fixed-window downloads, repository/global storage, add/replace/remove/search, secret and injection scanning, timestamps, and the best test evidence. With exact Pi 0.83 packages forced, TypeScript and all 40 upstream test files/732 tests passed, and the real Pi 0.83 Host loaded nine commands without an Extension error. The fork will retain and harden atomic Markdown mutation, bounded index/topic files, repository/global scopes, SQLite search, content scanning, metadata, migration, and recovery. It will remove periodic every-N-turn transcript review, compaction/shutdown mining, failure diaries, generated skills, session archive/search, emoji notifications, current modal UI, and basename-only project identity. Project memory is local plaintext, visible through compact Saved/Recalled transcript records and a standard non-floating /memory Command Dialog with view/edit/delete/toggle; it is fallible context, never policy or truth. The remaining maintainer decision is the fresh-install write policy: A quiet in-band auto memory, where the main Agent may save one durable fact during normal work without periodic review; or B explicit-only, where a write occurs only after wording such as remember this. Both keep immediate explicit memory, replace corrections atomically, use repository-local scope by default, require explicit wording for global scope, avoid one-off task state, and expose every write. comments.text: Source-backed UI recommendation pending maintainer confirmation, 2026-08-01 — Claude Code evidence supports three distinct reading layers: the default conversation is optimized for understanding, the detailed transcript is optimized for inspection while still filtering noise, and a separate durable session record is optimized for recovery and export. Visible content is classified by human meaning rather than provider message role. One tool or foreground-Agent operation owns its queued, waiting, running, success, failure, rejected, and canceled states; live progress updates that record in place. Consecutive low-impact exploration may collapse into a semantic activity summary, while edits, other consequential mutations, failures, and user-action requirements must remain visible. Successful internal helper tools may render nothing, and duplicate expressions of the same fact should have one visible owner. Foreground Agent work leaves a compact expandable operation record. Background work uses a compact launch record, temporary near-editor running status, an Agents or Tasks Command Dialog for full control, and one terminal completion, failure, stop, or needs-input summary in the main conversation. Todo state and routine Todo updates do not enter the transcript. BTW lives in its Command Dialog and may keep session-local BTW history, but never enters the main conversation. Informational system noise and recovered retries disappear; user-affecting warnings, errors, compaction, interruption, recovery, and permission outcomes remain. comments.text: Feasibility correction and recommendation pending maintainer confirmation, 2026-08-01 — Semantic grouping is not a native Pi 0.83 transcript facility. Without forking Pi, it is feasible only as a Pi Stuff-owned projection: collect consecutive calls from owned or overridden read-only tools, hide their individual transcript rows, and append one persistent summary. Recommended combined direction: keep the main transcript permanently bounded and use a Tool Details Command Dialog for full content. Ctrl+O would open the latest group or operation, let the user select one constituent operation and scroll only that output, then Esc back to the unchanged transcript. This can be implemented without a Pi fork through public custom-UI APIs; using Ctrl+O requires an explicit Pi Stuff keybinding change that removes the Host global-expand binding before registering the focused inspector. comments.text: Confirmed 2026-08-02 — After a current official-source audit of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Pi, the mechanism map is refined without changing the Pi-as-Host boundary. Pi is the foundation. Pi Stuff has five product blocks: (1) work organization and Agent coordination, combining multi-Agent execution with Todo, BTW, background work, steering, interruption, and attention routing; (2) supervision and interaction UI; (3) continuity across context limits and sessions, combining Pi sessions/branching/compaction and explicit instructions with Agent-written memory; (4) safety and recoverability, explicitly separating dangerous-action policy/approval from checkpoint/rewind of ordinary file edits; and (5) the extensible capability layer built from owned forks, tools, skills, hooks, MCP, and Pi packages. GitHub, browser control, deployment, review, and other tool-composed jobs are children or acceptance scenarios of block 5, not peer product blocks. The previous separate multi-Agent and work-control blocks are merged; safety/recoverability becomes the previously missing top-level block. Research record: /tmp/pi-stuff-coding-agent-capability-map.md. The next high-level topic is the user-visible recovery promise, not its implementation details.

comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text: Confirmed 2026-08-02 — Safe recovery belongs in the default Pi Stuff installation as the second half of the safety-and-recoverability block. Recovery is automatic and quiet: each user request establishes a recognizable recovery point without requiring a manual save. From a prior request, the user can restore Agent-made local code changes only, conversation only, or both; recovery survives session resume and compaction, previews affected files, preserves pre-existing and later user edits, stops on ambiguous conflicts instead of silently overwriting them, and creates an undo point before applying a restore. Conversation branching remains available when the user wants to preserve the current route and try another. Recovery does not claim to reverse external APIs, databases, deployments, or other remote side effects; those remain governed before execution by the separate safety policy. Unlike current Claude Code, Pi Stuff must not silently leave background subagent edits outside the product promise: writing Agents must either participate in a defined recovery domain or work in isolation that can be discarded safely. Healthy checkpointing adds no statusline or persistent UI. Exact panel layout and keys remain later UI decisions and require a real Pi/HTML preview under the established UI process.

comments.text: Confirmed 2026-08-02 — The extensible capability layer follows Claude Code local-terminal architecture while preserving Pi as Host. It has three user-facing tiers. (1) Always-available local core: keep Pi file/read/search/edit/shell tools and add owned-fork web/document reading plus code-intelligence tools so ordinary URL/search/PDF and symbol/diagnostic work is directly usable. (2) On-demand reusable expertise: use Pi native Agent Skills with progressive loading and automatic or explicit invocation; do not create a second workflow system or promote each skill-enabled job into a product block. (3) Opt-in external connections: ship a silent connection substrate with zero servers/accounts enabled, support project/user scopes and explicit authentication, and defer/search large tool catalogs so unused connections do not consume every prompt. Specific GitHub, issue tracker, database, monitoring, browser, or communication services are child connections, not peer capabilities. Pi Extensions provide lifecycle hooks and Pi Packages provide packaging, enable/disable, install and update; Pi Stuff will not build a second hook framework, plugin platform, or marketplace. Claude cloud/outer surfaces such as interactive browser/computer use, Remote Control, hosted artifacts, Slack/mobile surfaces and persistent cloud routines are not default Pi Stuff capabilities; they may remain optional external tools/packages. Healthy capability infrastructure adds no statusline and all tool results use the already accepted unified transcript renderer; exact connection/settings UI will later follow Claude behavior through real Pi TUI evidence and HTML review. Package selection remains subject to mature-Package research, an owned fork, provenance, trimming, and real Pi/Bun validation.

comments.text: Claude-completeness audit correction, 2026-08-02 — Three local-terminal mechanisms are added inside the already accepted work-organization block rather than becoming new product blocks. Second, structured questions: the Agent may pause only for a genuinely non-discoverable, materially outcome-changing choice and present one focused question through the shared non-floating Command Dialog; routine ambiguity is resolved autonomously. Third, background commands and monitoring: long tests, builds, servers and filtered log/event watches can move to the background while the conversation continues, with list/output/stop/attach control and coalesced completion/failure notices. These follow current Claude Code local behavior and close gaps Pi intentionally leaves to Extensions. No statusline, floating job window, separate agent_bg implementation, or duplicate task manager is inherited from upstream candidates; Agent delegation remains owned by the selected pi-subagents fork. Exact Package choices remain pending mature-Package audits and real Pi/Bun validation. A default /doctor-style health check will report missing/degraded owned capabilities through a Skill/UI surface rather than each package adding persistent chrome.

comments.author: JC Zhang
comments.text: Confirmed safety behavior, 2026-08-02 — The maintainer chooses an unrestricted-working default with a safety backstop, now mapped to current Claude Code Auto behavior rather than YOLO/bypassPermissions. Routine reads, edits and ordinary commands inside the current workspace proceed without approval; safe read-only network use and already-authorized connections also proceed. One central pre-action policy covers built-in file/shell tools, owned-fork tools, MCP calls and every foreground/background subagent. Deterministic hard rules run first for critical paths and unmistakable catastrophe (filesystem root/home destruction, raw devices, fork bombs, protected credentials/config, unsafe fetch-and-execute and equivalent obfuscation); project configuration may tighten but never loosen these rules. Actions outside the workspace or against external/shared state—destructive deletion, force push/protected branch, production deploy/migration, permissions/IAM, mass cloud deletion, secret transmission, or unknown infrastructure—are blocked for a safe alternative or routed to a bounded safety review using the user request, project instructions and proposed action but no untrusted tool output. Only when the action is still necessary and the user did not already give exact authority does the shared non-floating Command Dialog ask. Explicit user boundaries such as do-not-push are treated as blocks, but durable deny rules—not transcript memory—provide hard guarantees. The default is not a claim of perfect safety. Healthy safety infrastructure has no statusline; denials are visible with reason and can be reviewed/retried. OS-level workspace/network sandboxing should be used where available and must fail visibly to policy review rather than silently disappearing. Exact owned-fork base and runtime gates remain under package audit.

title: Move BTW onto Pi's full host-managed side-call path when available
description: Pi 0.83 lets an extension resolve the active registered model and provider authentication without changing the transcript, but it does not expose a public host-managed model-call path that also remains transcript-free. The shipped BTW fork therefore performs the isolated provider call directly: it preserves the active model, registry authentication, tool-free context, independent cancellation, and transcript isolation, but it cannot inherit Pi Host provider lifecycle/context hooks or Host retry and transport settings. Revisit this task only when Pi exposes a suitable public seam; do not fork Pi or weaken BTW isolation to obtain it.
acceptance_criteria: BTW uses a public Pi Host API for an independent tools-disabled side question while preserving zero main-transcript writes, zero main-context writes, independent cancellation, active model/auth resolution, streaming, and current Command Dialog behavior. Provider lifecycle/context hooks plus Host retry/transport settings are exercised by real-host tests. No Pi fork is introduced.
